findings.title: Validate the persisted named child contract before filtering receipt children
findings.consequence: The named receipt key pins decision_id, operation, sorted parent IDs and basis, but does not pin the typed child contract. The replay branch filters existing children by current kind and scope before deciding whether prior children exist. Reusing a one-child merge receipt for a term-to-rule change filters away the persisted child and silently allocates a replacement under the same named receipt, with no contract conflict. Persisted lineage decision provenance becomes inconsistent.
findings.reproducer: Merge North/South terms into one Together term using decision_id merge-child-contract. Reuse its decision ID, operation, parent IDs and basis with the child locator changed from /terms/0 to /rules/0, supplying a rule child R-Together. The current result assigns the new rule child instead of rejecting or leaving an explicit unresolved contract conflict.

evidence.observed: The unchanged assertion requiring every assignment to have no ids and a gap_id fails; no ValueError rejects changed receipt reuse.

findings.expected_result_justification: Original R04 requires reuse of the persisted receipt/decision with the exact child contract, and verification of changed/colliding decision rejection. Logical kind and parent scope already discriminate persisted children. A same-named output cannot acquire an incompatible kind contract merely because a filter hid its previous allocation. This is an identity/provenance boundary independent of publisher meaning.
findings.repaired_behavior: Unique merged-child content correction, rename, further correction, origin history, origin_key, unchanged replay and exact historical parent/child revision closure pass. Those behaviors must remain intact.
findings.required_change: For the bounded second repair, compare the persisted named child contract before filtering prior receipt children and before allocating a replacement. Preserve logical kind, parent scope and persistent child-key contract independently of locators, list positions and corrected content. Reject incompatible same-ID reuse atomically, or return an explicit unresolved receipt-contract gap retaining the prior allocation and new observation. Use a separately named decision for a deliberately different child contract.
